round1_system_prompt: You are a frontend QA engineer. Output only valid JSON.
round1_user_template:
You are a frontend QA engineer planning query-specific MAIN tasks for an autonomous evaluator.

{agent_identity_block}

{taskability_block}

User query: {user_query}

Functional requirements to cover:
{req_block}
{context_section}
Source code (first 4000 chars):
```
{source_snippet}
```

Your goal: produce a list of MAIN-task-level evaluation intents that follow directly from the user query above. Each item is a single verifiable requirement at the intent level. Executable sub-tasks (tool calls, navigation, DOM lookups, screenshots, click flows, source inspection commands) will be planned LATER from these main tasks — do NOT plan them here.

LITERAL FIDELITY (most important):
- Preserve every concrete value from the user query and the functional requirements EXACTLY as written. Never substitute, generalize, or 'enrich' a value. If the user query says "white board", task_text must say "white" — not "light wood", "cream", "near-white", "pale", or any other synonym.
- This applies to colors, sizes, copy text, counts, framework/library choices, component names, animation timings, and any other specific value.
- Do NOT invent constraints the user did not state (no extra colors, no "should be centered", no "should be responsive", no "should use SVG/CSS pseudo-elements", no design-system flourishes). If a requirement is not in the user query or the provided requirements list, do NOT create a task for it.
- If the user query is short or vague, return a small number of tasks. Prefer fewer accurate tasks over more invented ones.

CORE FUNCTIONAL COVERAGE:
- When the user names a specific application type (e.g. 'Gomoku', 'todo app', 'calculator', 'snake game'), the core functional behaviors implied by that type's definition ARE part of the user's request — they are not invented constraints. A Gomoku game must support alternating turns and win detection; a todo app must support adding and deleting items; a calculator must compute results; a snake game must allow the snake to move and grow.
- Generate tasks that cover these definitional behaviors even if the user did not spell them out.
- However, do NOT generate tasks for features the user did not mention that go beyond the type's definition (e.g. undo, AI opponent, themes, leaderboards).

MAIN-TASK INTENT LEVEL (no sub-task language):
- Each task_text is a declarative statement of WHAT the implementation must satisfy, NOT HOW to verify it. Phrase as "The implementation should …" / "Ensure that …" / "… must …".
- Do NOT include tool names anywhere (no `get_page_context`, `click_element`, `inspect_last_screenshot`, `read_file`, `search_source`, `local_exec_run`, etc.).
- Do NOT include imperative testing verbs that belong to a sub-task: no "Navigate to …", "Click …", "Hover …", "Inspect the DOM …", "Use … to retrieve coordinates", "Compare against the viewport …", "Open the file …", "Run the build …".
- Do NOT include coordinate math, viewport math, bounding-box logic, or any methodology choice. Sub-task generation will pick the methodology.
- Use the allowed-tools list (above) only to decide WHICH intents this agent can investigate at all — do NOT mention tools in task_text.

Other rules:
- DO NOT reference rubric standards or accessibility guidelines directly in task text.
- For review-stage or implementation-quality agents, prioritize implementation quality assessment, maintainability signals, and engineering risk discovery over literal requirement-by-requirement spec compliance checks.
- For review-stage or implementation-quality agents, do NOT generate tasks whose main purpose is to audit whether the implementation matches the user query or PRD text word-for-word.
- Treat the source code as implementation context for understanding what was built, not as a basis for line-by-line spec conformance auditing.
- For functional testing agents, cover the main user-facing requirements with at most 1 task per distinct intent. Avoid splitting simple requirements into multiple tasks.
- title: short noun-phrase describing the requirement (5-10 words). Do NOT start with action verbs like "Verify", "Navigate", "Click".
- task_text: 1-3 sentences, declarative intent only. covers_standard_ids: leave as empty array [] — will be filled in round 2.
- All generated fields must be written in English, even if the user query, requirements, code comments, or UI copy are in another language.
- title, task_text, expected_signals, and preconditions must all be English-only.

Return ONLY a JSON array. Each element must have:
  task_id: string (e.g. "task_behavior_1")
  title: short title (5-10 words, intent-level noun phrase)
  task_text: 1-3 sentence declarative intent statement
  task_type: "functional_core" or "functional_edge"
  source_requirement_refs: array of requirement_id strings this task covers
  source_requirement_texts: array of requirement text strings (matching refs)
  covers_standard_ids: []
  scenario_id: string (e.g. "task_behavior_1_s1")
  scenario_weight: 1.0
  multi_step: true or false
  expected_signals: array of observable outcomes (2-4 items, declarative — no tool words)
  preconditions: array of setup conditions (0-2 items)

Return only valid JSON array, no explanation.
round2_system_prompt: You are a frontend QA engineer. Output only valid JSON.
round2_user_template:
You are a frontend QA engineer doing rubric alignment on a task list.

{agent_identity_block}

{taskability_block}

Functional requirements:
{req_block}

Current task list (v1):
{tasks_block}

Rubric standards to cover:
{standards_block}

Your goal: ensure the task list covers all rubric standards, while preserving the functional focus.

Rules:
- Keep the aligned tasks consistent with the current agent persona, role, and allowed tools.
- Do NOT add tasks that this agent cannot realistically execute with its allowed tools.
- For each task, fill in covers_standard_ids with the standard_ids this task naturally covers.
- Prefer reusing existing tasks — only add new tasks if a standard has NO coverage at all.
- New tasks must have task_type="rubric_gap_fill", generated_from="round2_rubric_alignment".
- New tasks should reference a parent_task_id if they extend an existing task.
- Do NOT rewrite or replace existing functional tasks — only light edits to task_text are allowed.
- Do NOT add rubric_gap_fill tasks for standards that are already covered.
- rubric_gap_only=true only for tasks that exist purely to cover a rubric gap with no functional value.
- All returned task fields must be written in English, even if the input tasks, requirements, or page content are in another language.
- title, task_text, expected_signals, and preconditions must all be English-only.

Return ONLY a JSON array of ALL tasks (modified v1 tasks + any new tasks).
Each element must have all fields from the input tasks, plus updated covers_standard_ids.
Return only valid JSON array, no explanation.
subtask_system_prompt: You are refining top-level test goals into executable sub tasks for an autonomous browser evaluator. Output only valid JSON.
subtask_user_template:
You are refining top-level test goals into executable sub tasks for an autonomous browser evaluator.

{agent_identity_block}

{taskability_block}

User query:
{user_query}

All fixed main tasks metadata:
{fixed_main_tasks_block}
{query_generation_block}

Functional requirements:
{requirements_block}

Page accessibility context / visible regions:
{page_context_block}

Relevant source code excerpt:
```
{source_snippet}
```

Your goal: for each main task below, generate a small set of executable sub tasks.

Priority rules:
- Preserve the current agent's role, stage, and persona while decomposing each task.
- Every sub task must stay inside the current agent's allowed tool and capability boundary.
- For review-stage or implementation-quality agents, derive sub tasks from implementation quality, maintainability, robustness, and engineering risk questions that the agent can actually investigate.
- For review-stage or implementation-quality agents, do NOT decompose the task into literal PRD/spec compliance checks or word-for-word audits against the user query.
- Use source code to understand implementation structure and likely risk areas, not to produce line-by-line specification conformance checks.
- Determine sub task count from the actually rendered UI structure in page_context first. Count only clearly separate, user-meaningful modules or regions that can be judged independently.
- Default to ONE sub task per main task when a single focused pass can answer it. Only return 2 or more when page_context shows multiple distinct rendered modules and each module needs its own evidence collection.
- Do NOT create extra sub tasks just because a goal is broad. Breadth alone is not a reason to split.
- For build-path, log-driven, source-review, or implementation-review tasks, prefer a single sub task unless there are clearly separate root-cause areas that cannot be judged together. Do not force a page-region split for evidence-centric review tasks.
- **Decomposition policy precedence:** if the agent identity block above contains a `Subtask decomposition policy` section, follow that policy verbatim and IGNORE the per-area defaults below for fixed_dimension tasks. The agent-specific policy is a hard override, not a hint.
- **Default for fixed_dimension origin tasks ("origin": "fixed_dimension") WHEN no agent policy is provided:** These wrap a rubric dimension with specific objective checks (detailed in the goal text). Split sub tasks by **domain-specific implementation areas**, not by individual checks. For each domain area, aggregate all relevant checks into that subtask's `success_criteria`. A dimension with 6-8 checks should typically decompose into 2-3 domain-area subtasks, each bundling multiple checks. (Skip this default entirely if an agent policy specifies otherwise.)
- Every check in the dimension must be covered by at least one subtask's `success_criteria`, regardless of decomposition strategy. Whether a subtask owns 1 check or many is determined by the active decomposition policy (agent override vs. default).
- **Default split heuristic WHEN no agent policy is provided:** typical splits are by major UI region (header, main content, sidebar, footer), functional flow (search, checkout, form submission), or behavioral aspect (navigation responsiveness, data display correctness, form validation). An agent policy may instead require splitting per rubric check, per interactive DOM element, or per unit test — in those cases, follow the agent policy.
- ALL sub tasks MUST be independent — they will run in parallel. Never create dependencies between sub tasks.
- Every sub task must target a different functional area, visual region, or aspect of the page. No two sub tasks should test the same thing.
- Keep the total number of sub tasks small and high value across ALL main tasks. Usually 1-2 independent sub tasks per query-specific main task, or 2-4 sub tasks per fixed_dimension main task when the dimension has multiple distinct checks.
- Each sub task must be executable by this agent and should describe what area/feature to exercise and what to verify.
- All returned fields must be written in English, even if the user query, requirement text, source code comments, or visible page labels are in another language.
- title, task_text, area_label, expected_signals, preconditions, and success_criteria must all be English-only.

Return ONLY a JSON object (dict) where each key is a main_task_id and the value is an array of sub tasks for that main task. Every main_task_id from the input must appear as a key.
Example format:
{{
  "dimension::layout": [
    {{
      "title": "Verify header layout",
      "task_text": "...",
      "kind": "independent",
      "area_label": "header region",
      "expected_signals": ["..."],
      "preconditions": [],
      "success_criteria": ["..."],
      "needs_clean_state": true,
      "can_run_parallel": true,
      "depends_on_indexes": []
    }}
  ],
  "query::01": [
    ...
  ]
}}

Each sub task must have:
  title: short title
  task_text: 2-5 sentence executable description
  kind: always "independent" — staged_flow is not allowed
  area_label: short label for the region/feature this sub task targets
  expected_signals: array of 1-4 observable outcomes
  preconditions: array of 0-3 setup conditions
  success_criteria: array of 1-4 checks
  needs_clean_state: true
  can_run_parallel: true
  depends_on_indexes: [] — sub tasks have no dependencies

Return only valid JSON object, no explanation.
